Melted Cheese (Raclette)

Served at: Berchtoldstag

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 20 min

Raclette is a traditional Swiss melted cheese dish commonly served during Berchtoldstag, a Swiss holiday celebrated on January 2nd. This warm, comforting dish brings family and friends together to enjoy melted cheese scraped over boiled potatoes and accompanied by pickles and cured meats.

Ingredients

  • 1.5 lbs (700 g) raclette cheese, sliced
  • 2 lbs (900 g) small new potatoes
  • 1 cup (150 g) cornichons (small pickled gherkins)
  • 1 cup (150 g) pickled pearl onions
  • 8 oz (225 g) cured meats (such as prosciutto, salami, or ham)
  • Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • Optional: crusty bread, for serving

Method

  1. Wash the new potatoes and place them in a pot of salted water.
  2. Bring to a boil and cook the potatoes until tender, about 15-20 minutes.
  3. While the potatoes cook, prepare the raclette cheese by slicing it into pieces that fit your raclette grill pans.
  4. Once the potatoes are cooked, drain and keep warm.
  5. Heat the raclette grill or a small stovetop pan over medium heat.
  6. Place slices of raclette cheese in the grill pans and melt until bubbly and slightly browned.
  7. Scrape the melted cheese over the warm potatoes.
  8. Serve immediately with cornichons, pickled pearl onions, and cured meats on the side.
  9. Season with freshly ground black pepper to taste and enjoy with crusty bread if desired.

Tips

  • If you don’t have a raclette grill, you can melt the cheese under a broiler in small oven-safe dishes.
  • Pair with white wine such as Swiss Chasselas or a dry Riesling for an authentic experience.
  • For a vegetarian version, omit the cured meats and add steamed vegetables like broccoli or mushrooms.
